title: Rapid integrability scan for low-latency model entrants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a lightweight, repeatable scan that ranks newly surfaced low-latency model entrants by how quickly and cheaply they can be served on Redwood (hosted + edge variants).

Motivation: the market is seeing many narrow, optimized models that claim sub-50ms tail latency on certain hardware. We need a pragmatic rubric to triage which entrants are worth engineering integration effort (kernel selection, quantization support, memory profiling) and which should be funneled to a longlist for later procurement. The deliverable is an "Integration Readiness Index (IRI)" and a reproducible harness that outputs a compact scorecard and integration checklist.

Scope: vendors/OSS builds that advertise low latency for short-context use. Focus on text-generation encoder-decoder and causal-decoder families under 8B params (initial pass). Excludes multimodal and speech models in this ticket.

Success metric: for the first 8 candidates produce IRI scores + human review notes; have 2 candidates promoted to ENG spike for integration within two cycles, and provide the PM/ENG prioritization memo for capacity and procurement decisions.
tasks: Design IRI rubric (API compat, memory footprint, kv-cache read/write, quantization tolerance, observed latency distribution)
Implement bench harness repo skeleton and CI job (synthetic request generator + warmup patterns)
Run baseline: 8 candidate models across 3 hardware profiles (T4-like, A10-like, H100-like simulated), capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost estimates
Produce one-page scorecard per model and compile a summary matrix
Share findings with Eng (runtime) for kernel-level red flags and with Legal for license/redistribution review
Recommend next-step classification: Spike, Watch, Reject, or Procurement-Ready
acceptance_criteria: IRI rubric doc stored in Drive + Confluence linkable summary
Bench harness runs reproducibly in CI and logs to our benchmarking S3 bucket
Scorecard includes at minimum: API compatibility notes, memory footprint at 2048 and 4096 context, quantization artifacts, p95/p99 latencies, token cost estimate, and integration-risk flags
Two candidate models flagged for ENG spike or Dedicated trial
PM memo summarizing business/competitive implications and recommended follow-up path
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: Draft IRI rubric shared with @Logan Chen and runtime leads. Proposed weightings: latency 30%, memory 20%, API compat 20%, tooling/training footprint 15%, license risk 15%.
2026-03-04 — Eng feedback: runtime notes that KV cache behavior on decoder-only models may hide p99 regressions; suggested adding a forced cold-start test and prefix-heavy traffic pattern.
2026-03-06 — Legal review requested for candidate vendor A (license indicates non-commercial restrictions). Marked as 'Watch' until clarifying terms.
2026-03-08 — Bench harness PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/214 — includes synthetic runner and CSV score export. Needs ENG review for CI credentials.

2026-03-09 — Product review: prioritized list updated after initial runs; Candidate 3 shows strong p95 but fails memory budget on A10-like; flagged for 'Spike' because quantized variant might remediate.
2026-03-10 — Blocker: gated by access to quantized weights for Candidate 5. Action: SEs to request artifact or provide conversion instructions. Assigned to Logan.
